title: Tribal Inheritances
overview: Joshua 19 details the allotment of land to seven tribes of Israel—Simeon, Zebulun, Issachar, Asher, Naphtali, Dan, and the special inheritance given to Joshua himself. This chapter completes the distribution of the Promised Land, emphasizing God’s faithfulness in fulfilling His covenant promises to the descendants of Abraham. The precise listing of cities and boundaries underscores the orderly and divinely guided nature of Israel’s settlement. It also highlights the unity and diversity within the nation, as each tribe receives its portion according to God’s plan. This chapter serves as a vital link in the narrative of Israel’s establishment in Canaan, showing the practical outworking of God’s promise through faithful leadership and divine guidance.
structure:
**Verses 1-9: Inheritance of Simeon.** This section describes the land allotted to the tribe of Simeon, noting that their inheritance was within the territory of Judah due to Judah’s large portion.

**Verses 10-16: Inheritance of Zebulun.** The chapter outlines the borders and cities given to Zebulun, emphasizing the detailed boundaries and the twelve cities with their villages.

**Verses 17-23: Inheritance of Issachar.** This portion lists the cities and borders of Issachar’s territory, highlighting the sixteen cities and their villages.

**Verses 24-31: Inheritance of Asher.** The land assigned to Asher is described with its extensive borders reaching to the sea and including twenty-two cities.

**Verses 32-39: Inheritance of Naphtali.** Naphtali’s territory is detailed with its borders, fenced cities, and nineteen cities with their villages.

**Verses 40-48: Inheritance of Dan.** The land allotted to Dan is described, including their conquest of Leshem, which they renamed Dan.

**Verses 49-51: Inheritance to Joshua.** The chapter concludes with the special inheritance given to Joshua himself, fulfilling God’s promise to provide for His servant.

keyVerses.text: Out of the portion of the children of Judah was the inheritance of the children of Simeon: for the part of the children of Judah was too much for them: therefore the children of Simeon had their inheritance within the inheritance of them.
keyVerses.significance: This verse highlights the practical arrangement of tribal inheritances, showing God’s provision even when land portions varied. It reflects the unity and cooperation among tribes under God’s sovereign plan.

keyVerses.text: And the coast of the children of Dan went out too little for them: therefore the children of Dan went up to fight against Leshem, and took it, and smote it with the edge of the sword, and possessed it, and dwelt therein, and called Leshem, Dan, after the name of Dan their father.
keyVerses.significance: This verse illustrates the initiative and faithfulness of the tribe of Dan in securing their inheritance, demonstrating the necessity of active obedience in claiming God’s promises.

keyVerses.text: According to the word of the LORD they gave him the city which he asked, even Timnathserah in mount Ephraim: and he built the city, and dwelt therein.
keyVerses.significance: This verse shows God’s faithfulness to Joshua personally, rewarding his leadership with a special inheritance, reinforcing the theme of divine blessing upon obedience.

keyVerses.text: These are the inheritances, which Eleazar the priest, and Joshua the son of Nun, and the heads of the fathers of the tribes of the children of Israel, divided for an inheritance by lot in Shiloh before the LORD, at the door of the tabernacle of the congregation. So they made an end of dividing the country.
keyVerses.significance: This closing verse emphasizes the divine authority and priestly oversight in the land division, underscoring that the allotment was done under God’s direct guidance and blessing.

characters.name: Joshua
characters.description: The leader of Israel who oversaw the division of the Promised Land. He receives a special inheritance in this chapter, demonstrating God’s reward for faithful service.

characters.name: Eleazar the Priest
characters.description: The high priest who assisted Joshua in dividing the land by lot, representing the priestly authority and God’s presence in the process.

characters.name: Tribes of Israel
characters.description: The seven tribes receiving their land inheritances: Simeon, Zebulun, Issachar, Asher, Naphtali, Dan, and the tribe of Joshua. Each tribe’s portion reflects God’s sovereign distribution.

themes.description: The chapter demonstrates God’s faithfulness in fulfilling His promise to give the land to Israel, showing that His covenant is reliable and sure.
The detailed allotment by lot reflects God’s just and orderly nature in distributing blessings among His people.
The tribe of Dan’s conquest of Leshem highlights the necessity of active obedience and faith in claiming God’s promises.
Though each tribe receives a distinct inheritance, the chapter emphasizes the unity of Israel as a nation under God’s plan.

historicalContext: This chapter is set in the late Bronze Age, around the 15th century BC, during Israel’s settlement in Canaan after the Exodus from Egypt. The land division reflects ancient Near Eastern customs of tribal land allotments, where land was a primary inheritance and source of identity. The political situation involved Israel establishing itself among Canaanite city-states, requiring military conquest and divine guidance. The use of casting lots was a common ancient practice to discern God’s will in decisions, reflecting Israel’s trust in divine sovereignty. Geographically, the territories span from the Negev in the south to the northern borders near Tyre and Sidon, encompassing diverse landscapes and strategic locations.

theologicalInterpretations.description: Reformed theology sees this chapter as illustrating God’s sovereign providence in the distribution of blessings. The allotment by lot signifies God’s control over all aspects of life, including inheritance and leadership.
Dispensationalists interpret the land division as a literal fulfillment of God’s covenant with Israel, emphasizing the future prophetic significance of these territories in eschatological events.
Early Church Fathers often allegorized the land allotments as representing spiritual inheritance in Christ, seeing Joshua as a type of Christ leading believers into the promised rest.

crossReferences.connection: Details the command to divide the land by lot, providing background to the procedure described in Joshua 19.
Speaks of God dividing the nations by the number of the children of Israel, linking divine sovereignty to the allotment of land.
Mentions the pleasant inheritance given by God, echoing the theme of God’s provision in Joshua 19.
Stephen references the division of the land under Joshua’s leadership, affirming the historical reality of these events.
Uses Joshua’s leadership and the land allotment as a type of the spiritual rest believers enter through faith.

application: Trust in God’s sovereign provision when facing decisions, knowing He directs outcomes according to His perfect will.
Actively pursue the promises God has given, as the tribe of Dan did, with faith and obedience.
Recognize the importance of unity within the body of Christ despite diverse roles and blessings.
Value the spiritual inheritance believers have in Christ as the true Promised Land.
Honor God’s appointed leaders and the order He establishes in the church and community.
Be grateful for God’s faithfulness in fulfilling His promises, encouraging perseverance in faith.
conclusion: Joshua 19 stands as a testament to God’s faithfulness in fulfilling His covenant promises through orderly and divinely guided land distribution. The chapter highlights the importance of obedience, unity, and trust in God’s sovereign plan. It reminds believers today that God’s blessings are purposeful and that active faith is required to possess them fully. The special inheritance given to Joshua underscores the reward of faithful leadership. This chapter encourages Christians to embrace their spiritual inheritance in Christ and to live in harmony under God’s sovereign authority.
timeline: c. 1406-1399 BC - Israel’s settlement and division of Canaan under Joshua’s leadership

outline.heading: Inheritance of Simeon
outline.description: The tribe of Simeon receives its inheritance within Judah’s territory, illustrating God’s provision despite limited land.

outline.heading: Inheritance of Zebulun
outline.description: Zebulun’s borders and cities are detailed, emphasizing the comprehensive nature of the allotment.

outline.heading: Inheritance of Issachar
outline.description: Issachar’s territory is described with its cities and boundaries, showing God’s precise distribution.

outline.heading: Inheritance of Asher
outline.description: Asher’s land extends to the sea and includes many cities, highlighting the diversity of Israel’s inheritance.

outline.heading: Inheritance of Naphtali
outline.description: Naphtali’s territory includes fenced cities and villages, demonstrating established settlements.

outline.heading: Inheritance of Dan and Joshua
outline.description: Dan’s limited land leads to conquest of Leshem, renamed Dan, and Joshua receives his special inheritance, concluding the division.
